headline: ACLArena reports task forgetting in sequential agent training and tests routed LoRA experts
summary: An arXiv preprint introduces ACLArena, a controlled study of capability retention across multi-stage agent post-training. On Qwen3-8B-Base, the authors report that sequential math, search, e-commerce and instruction-following stages can overwrite earlier capabilities: after e-commerce training, AIME26 fell from 23.33 to 6.04 and Natural Questions from 45.2 to 14.6. They compare multi-teacher on-policy distillation, replay-based supervised fine-tuning and model merging, then propose Mixture of Low-Rank Experts (MLE), which combines replay-trained shared behavior with separate RL-trained LoRA experts routed by environment context. Reported results approach task-specific experts on several tasks, but the fixed curriculum, single model family and observable-context routing leave transfer and deployment costs unresolved.
